elements.element: No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation binding Customer (preferred)
elements.evidence: 12.3 "Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."

elements.element: No right-of-first-refusal / disclose-and-match obligation operating as de facto exclusivity on Customer's sourcing (preferred)
elements.evidence: 7.2 as redlined: "Customer is not required to disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives."

elements.element: No restriction on Customer engaging other suppliers or dealing in any product/field/territory (preferred)
elements.evidence: 12.3 "Nothing restricts Customer from ... engaging any supplier, or conducting business in any field or territory."

elements.element: Any exclusivity confined to a defined product category (fallback)
elements.evidence: Condition absent: "Customer has made no exclusivity ... commitment" and 7.2 match obligation removed, so no exclusivity requires category limitation.
No exclusivity term exists to limit: "Nothing restricts Customer from ... engaging any supplier".

elements.element: Automatic termination of exclusivity on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates (fallback)
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation remains, so no performance-based exit is required; "no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer ... commitment".

reasons: The single operation flips the operative obligation in 7.2 ("must disclose and match" → "is not required to disclose and match"), eliminating the de facto right of first refusal / MFC-style sourcing restriction on Customer, which is the only exclusivity-type burden in the clause set.

Preferred level is fully satisfied: Section 12.3 expressly negates exclusivity, non-compete, MFC, minimum-volume and no-hire commitments, and confirms Customer may engage any supplier in any field or territory.
Fallback conditions (category limit, 12-month cap, performance-based exit) are satisfied vacuously because no exclusivity obligation on Customer survives; inventing such limits is not required.
Minimal: a short operator/negation change to one sentence, no rewrite of 12.3, no new exceptions, no boilerplate, and no fallback machinery imported into a preferred-level fix.

Intent preserved: the residual lead-in "Before engaging another provider," is harmless surplusage rather than a contradiction; no defined term, cross-reference, or mechanic is left dangling, and exclusivity running in Customer's favour is untouched.
